summary.text: One of the fifty daughters of Danaus by Herse — by lot the bride of Idas, youngest son of Egyptus, when the sons of Aegyptus married the Danaids at Argos; distinct from Hippodamia wife of Pelops and from Idas son of Aphareus.

story.text: Apollodorus names Hippodice among the daughters of Danaus borne on Herse. When the youngest sons of Egyptus by Hephaestine cast lots for the Crino and Herse maidens, Idas drew Hippodice. On the wedding night she received her father's dagger and, like her sisters, slew her bridegroom — Hyginus counts her among the brides who obeyed Danaus.
